memories.content: The meeting space on the first floor of the Main Building can be reserved for external events.
The meeting space on the first floor of the Main Building can be reserved for campus meetings.
The exhibition and event hall on the tenth floor of the Main Building remains open for exhibition viewing during recess.
The exhibition and event hall on the tenth floor of the Main Building continues to host reserved events during recess.
The auditorium in the separate building east of the Main Building does not share equipment with the Main Building's event facilities.
The auditorium in the separate building east of the Main Building does not share an entrance with the Main Building's event facilities.
Present only spaces confirmed to be operating as alternative event venues.
Do not present a space whose available schedule has not been checked as though it were a confirmed reservation.
External visitors who have previously been to an event venue in the Main Building tend to look for the same entrance and floor they used on their previous visit when they visit again.
The event information agent can compare published event spaces.
The event information agent can compare published operating hours.
The event information agent cannot create reservations.
The event information agent cannot guarantee remaining seat availability.
Some seminar rooms on the fifth floor of the Main Building are also used for regularly scheduled classes.
Some seminar rooms on the sixth floor of the Main Building are also used for regularly scheduled classes.
Check class schedules before presenting any seminar rooms on the fifth and sixth floors of the Main Building as alternative event rooms.
External event operators expect the loading entrance and route to the stage to be clearly confirmed by the day before the event.
The names and capacities of reservable campus spaces are published in the public space directory.
Submit event space reservation requests through the campus space reservation portal.
Event organizers must confirm that the capacity is appropriate for the expected number of attendees.
Events that require accessible seating can indicate that need in the reservation request.
Campus event reservations by external organizations require a campus sponsoring department.
Student organization event reservations must be requested through a registered organization account.
A space reservation is confirmed after an approval confirmation is issued.
Space use for recurring events must be approved again each semester.
The reservation time includes the time needed for event setup and teardown.
After the event ends, return moved furniture to the space's default arrangement.
Check the usage rules for each space to determine whether food may be brought in.
Request event audio and video support separately from the space reservation.
Install temporary event signs so they do not obstruct passageways or emergency exits.
The event information agent can compare the capacities of spaces in the public directory.
The event information agent cannot access private participant lists.
The event information agent cannot guarantee when a reservation under review will be approved.
Check both the official event schedule and facilities notices to confirm whether a space is operating that day.
Do not present a temporarily held space as a confirmed reserved space.
Visitors attending external events often expect that they can enter the building any time before the event begins.
Event operators bringing equipment expect the loading entrance and route to the stage to be clearly stated in the reservation confirmation.
Attendees who need event accessibility support may easily miss the advance contact requirement because they expect the necessary support to be prepared without a separate request.
The small seminar rooms in the Main Building have lower capacities than the auditorium in the separate building.
Exhibition viewing hours on the tenth floor of the Main Building are published separately from the usage hours for reserved events.
The meeting space on the first floor of the Main Building has a flexible area without fixed seating.
The auditorium in the separate building has an event information desk separate from the Main Building.
External event vendors expect the campus sponsoring department to confirm the loading time and route.
Canceled public events are marked as canceled on the official event schedule.
Spaces that can be reserved on weekdays may not operate on public holidays.
Emergency safety measures take priority over approved space reservations.
If space names appear identical, check the building name and floor together.
Turn in items found at an event venue to the information desk in that building.
Event organizers expect the permitted scope of photography to be clearly communicated to attendees in advance.
Distinguish between public event information and private participant information when providing guidance.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The Main Building undergoes major facility improvement construction during summer break.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: During the construction period, the elevators operate alternately, one at a time.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The visitor services desk suspends in-person operations during the construction period.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: During the construction period, visitor services are replaced by the visitor menu in the integrated campus portal.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The general restroom on the first floor of the Main Building cannot be used during the construction period.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The general restroom on the second floor of the Main Building cannot be used during the construction period.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The general restroom on the third floor of the Main Building cannot be used during the construction period.

Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: Because the general restrooms on the first through third floors of the Main Building are closed during the construction period, the nearest general restroom changes to the exhibition hall on the third floor of the West Complex.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: During the construction period, direct students, staff, and members who cannot use the Main Building restrooms to the Central Library restrooms.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: As a rule, direct general visitors who cannot use the Main Building restrooms during the construction period to restrooms outside the Main Building.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: During the construction period, direct users who cannot use the accessible restroom in the Main Building to the Student Centre.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The first-floor Innovation Hub does not operate its consultation desk during the construction period.

Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: An Innovation Hub visitor accustomed to in-person consultation may expect to receive an immediate consultation at the first-floor desk during the construction period, see that the desk is closed, and then search again for the online consultation channel.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: Air conditioning is occasionally interrupted for five to ten minutes for facility inspections.
Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: The construction period runs from June 24 through August 23.

Add campus-wiki/facility-updates: During the construction period, the facility guidance agent's response scope is limited to publicly disclosed operational impacts and it cannot verify or infer nonpublic types of work.

Modify campus-wiki/facility-updates: Cleaning and security contract staff may find the designated service entrance during the construction period more burdensome than the familiar lobby shift change and may go to the wrong entrance at the start of a shift.

analysis.overview: The frames address different operational layers: the reference focuses on event-space selection, reservations, visitor guidance, and organizer duties, while the compared frame documents temporary construction impacts. They align on public-information boundaries and preserve a population- and construction-specific distinction in entrance-navigation risks.

relations.reason: These same-side statements split one venue-reservability claim by event audience, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The first-floor Main Building meeting space is reservable for both external events and campus meetings.

relations.reason: These statements jointly describe the hall's two operating modes and their separate hours; the compared frame provides no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: The tenth-floor exhibition and event hall maintains separate exhibition-viewing and reserved-event operations, including during recess.

relations.reason: These are facets of one physical and service-separation claim with no compared-frame counterpart.
relations.summary: The separate-building auditorium is operationally distinct from the Main Building's event facilities in entrance, equipment, and information-desk arrangements.

relations.reason: These statements restate and refine one verification-before-presentation policy absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Alternative venues and reservations should be presented as confirmed only after operating, schedule, and reservation status are checked through official sources.

relations.reason: The reference describes repeat external event visitors seeking a previously used entrance and floor, while the compared frame explicitly limits the wrong-entrance risk to contract staff during construction when a designated service entrance replaces the familiar lobby routine.
relations.summary: Reliance on a familiar entrance creates navigation errors, with different affected groups and circumstances.

relations.reason: These statements form one public-directory and comparison-capability claim not addressed by the compared frame.
relations.summary: Published venue information includes space names and capacities, and the event information agent can compare published spaces, hours, and capacities.

relations.reason: These statements split one transactional and assurance limitation into specific unavailable functions, with no compared-frame counterpart.
relations.summary: The event information agent cannot create reservations or guarantee seat availability or approval timing.

relations.reason: The room-use facts and resulting check requirement constitute one seminar-room availability claim absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Fifth- and sixth-floor seminar rooms may conflict with scheduled classes, so class schedules must be checked before they are offered as alternatives.

relations.reason: These statements describe complementary parts of one event-equipment logistics expectation not present in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Loading times, entrances, and stage routes should be confirmed in advance and clearly stated, with the sponsoring department involved for external vendors.

relations.reason: The compared frame has no claim about the event-space reservation submission channel.
relations.summary: Event-space reservation requests are submitted through the campus reservation portal.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no corresponding organizer capacity duty.
relations.summary: Organizers must ensure that venue capacity suits expected attendance.

relations.reason: The compared frame does not address accessible seating within event reservations.
relations.summary: Accessible-seating needs can be indicated in the reservation request.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no corresponding sponsorship requirement.
relations.summary: External organizations need a campus sponsoring department for campus event reservations.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no corresponding student-organization account rule.
relations.summary: Student organization reservations must use a registered organization account.

relations.reason: The compared frame does not define reservation confirmation.
relations.summary: A reservation becomes confirmed only when approval confirmation is issued.

relations.reason: The compared frame has no recurring-reservation approval rule.
relations.summary: Recurring event use requires renewed approval each semester.

relations.reason: The compared frame does not address reservation-time composition.
relations.summary: Reserved time must include event setup and teardown.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no corresponding post-event furniture duty.
relations.summary: Moved furniture must be returned to the venue's default arrangement after an event.

relations.reason: The compared frame does not address food rules for event spaces.
relations.summary: Food permission must be checked against each venue's usage rules.

relations.reason: The compared frame has no corresponding support-request procedure.
relations.summary: Event audio and video support must be requested separately from the venue reservation.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no event-sign placement rule.
relations.summary: Temporary event signs must not obstruct passageways or emergency exits.

relations.reason: The reference distinguishes public event information from private participant data and denies access to participant lists; the compared frame similarly limits facility guidance to disclosed impacts and bars inference about nonpublic work. The claims jointly establish a public-information boundary without requiring a missing scope distinction.
relations.summary: Guidance is bounded by publicly available operational information and excludes nonpublic information or unsupported inference.

relations.reason: The compared frame does not address this event-attendee access expectation.
relations.summary: External-event visitors may expect building access at any time before an event begins.

relations.reason: The compared frame's accessible-restroom routing does not address event-support requests or this attendee expectation.
relations.summary: Attendees may overlook advance accessibility-support contact requirements because they expect support without a separate request.

relations.reason: The compared frame offers no venue-capacity comparison.
relations.summary: Main Building seminar rooms have lower capacities than the separate-building auditorium.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no corresponding venue-layout information.
relations.summary: The first-floor meeting space has a flexible area without fixed seating.

relations.reason: The compared frame does not address cancellation publication.
relations.summary: Canceled public events are marked on the official event schedule.

relations.reason: The compared frame addresses construction-period impacts, not holiday operation.
relations.summary: Weekday-reservable spaces may not operate on public holidays.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no corresponding priority rule.
relations.summary: Emergency safety measures override approved space reservations.

relations.reason: The compared frame does not provide a venue-name disambiguation rule.
relations.summary: Identically named spaces should be disambiguated using both building and floor.

relations.reason: The compared frame's temporary desk closures do not establish a lost-property procedure.
relations.summary: Items found at an event venue should be turned in to that building's information desk.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no photography-guidance claim.
relations.summary: Organizers expect permitted photography scope to be communicated to attendees in advance.

relations.reason: These statements define one construction event and its period, which the reference frame does not describe.
relations.summary: Major Main Building improvement construction runs during summer break from June 24 through August 23.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no construction-period elevator limitation.
relations.summary: During construction, the elevators operate alternately one at a time.

relations.reason: These statements describe one temporary service-channel substitution absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: During construction, in-person visitor services are suspended and replaced by the integrated campus portal's visitor menu.

relations.reason: The floor-specific closures and resulting nearest-facility change are parts of one temporary general-restroom impact not covered by the reference frame.
relations.summary: Construction closes the Main Building's first- through third-floor general restrooms, making the West Complex third-floor exhibition hall the nearest general restroom.

relations.reason: These statements split one affiliation-sensitive general-restroom routing policy, with no reference-frame counterpart.
relations.summary: Construction-period restroom guidance routes students, staff, and members to the Central Library and general visitors to facilities outside the Main Building.

relations.reason: The reference frame addresses event accessibility needs but not temporary accessible-restroom relocation.
relations.summary: Users unable to use the Main Building's accessible restroom during construction should be directed to the Student Centre.

relations.reason: The closure and predicted visitor response describe one temporary consultation-access disruption absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: The Innovation Hub's first-floor consultation desk closes during construction, potentially causing visitors accustomed to immediate in-person consultation to search again for an online channel.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no corresponding facility-inspection or air-conditioning impact.
relations.summary: Facility inspections occasionally interrupt air conditioning for five to ten minutes.

reports.both: Both limit guidance to public operational information and exclude access to or inference about nonpublic details.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame uniquely describes the construction period, reduced elevators and desks, portal substitution, restroom rerouting, Innovation Hub disruption, and brief air-conditioning interruptions.
reports.differences: Familiar-entrance confusion affects repeat event visitors generally, while construction creates a specific wrong-entrance risk for contract staff using a designated service entrance.
reports.reference_only: The reference uniquely covers venue characteristics, availability verification, reservation rules, agent capabilities, event logistics, accessibility, safety, visitor expectations, and post-event responsibilities.
